# The Freedom of a Clear Conscience

## Scripture

“So I strive always to keep my conscience clear before God and man.” — Acts 24:16

## Reflection

Paul stood before a governor who held his life in his hands, yet his concern was not the verdict but his conscience. That is a striking picture of manhood under pressure. We tend to measure ourselves by outcomes—whether the deal closed, whether the confrontation went well, whether anyone noticed. Paul measured himself by something quieter and more durable: was he clear before God and before people?

A man’s conscience is a gift, but it is not automatic. It can be seared by repeated compromise, or it can be kept tender through honest dealing. The word Paul uses is “strive”—this is deliberate, daily work. It means making the phone call you have been avoiding. It means telling your wife the truth about the account. It means apologizing to your son for the sharp word, even when he provoked it. It means refusing the shortcut that no one would ever discover.

Here is the good news: a clear conscience is not something you earn, but something grace restores. When we bring our failures into the light—confessing to God and, where needed, to the people we have wronged—the blood of Christ cleanses us and the weight lifts. Men carry enough legitimate burdens; we do not need to carry the unnecessary weight of a guilty conscience. Strive today for the small, hidden integrities that keep your heart soft and your walk unashamed.

## Prayer

Father, we ask for tender consciences and the courage to make things right quickly. Search us, expose what we have hidden, and let Your grace restore us. Keep us honest before You and before others, for Your glory. Amen.

## One-Line Application

Deal with the small dishonesty today—your conscience is worth more than the shortcut.
